prompt:
30s, 16:9, single take.

<<<image_1>>> is the main heroine: a slim damaged mannequin-girl with very long dirty-blond twin-tail hair partly covering the face, black sleeveless clothing, one wooden mannequin arm, one wooden mannequin leg, one living bare leg, and a slight limp. Keep her face, hair silhouette, body proportions, black clothing and mixed mannequin-human anatomy identical throughout. Her face must not morph.

<<<image_2>>> is the environment reference: endless white generative ether, made of suspended denoising dust, milky particulate haze, soft white floating matter and unfinished paint-like diffusion. Use it as the only environment.

<<<image_3>>> is a badly generated limping horse with too many legs.

<<<image_4>>> is a softly luminous slow-moving human figure.

<<<image_5>>> is a goat assembled from household objects.

<<<image_6>>> is a fish made of cloth and tile.

<<<image_7>>> is a rotating vortex-monument of human bodies.

<<<image_8>>> is a butterfly.

<<<image_9>>> is a rabbit with many ears.

<<<image_10>>> is a sheep-cloud with internal lightning.

<<<image_11>>> is a compact knot of birds moving as one flock-mass.

<<<image_12>>> is a horse that duplicates itself.

<<<image_13>>> is a pig made from ears.

<<<image_14>>> is a monkey made from yellow gloves.

<<<image_15>>> is a radish walking a dog.

<<<image_17>>> through <<<image_28>>> are badly generated people with flawed anatomy and drifting identity.

Summary: In an endless white field of unresolved generation, the heroine slowly turns in place while the camera circles her at closer range and the surrounding particulate matter repeatedly condenses into creatures, objects and flawed humans that only exist for moments before returning to dust.

0s–6s:
Open close on <<<image_1>>>’s face through the curtain of hair. The camera is already moving around her in a close handheld orbit. White grains drift between lens and subject. Pull just wide enough to show she stands alone in an infinite white ether with no edge and no architecture. She slowly rotates with the camera, trying to follow what is happening around her. The white field thickens and thins in clouds, as though ideas are trying to become matter.

6s–11s:
At the edge of frame, the grains compress into <<<image_3>>>, the many-legged limping horse. Stay close enough to feel the faulty anatomy: extra legs resolving in the wrong places, gait slipping, body struggling to complete itself. It limps across the background and disappears into the white.
Immediately after, <<<image_4>>> gathers from the same airborne grains near the heroine’s shoulder line. It resolves from face outward, stands with a loose tired posture, then recedes and is reclaimed by the ether.
The camera keeps the heroine in foreground while these beings form behind and beside her, then swings out briefly to catch their exits.

11s–16s:
Drop lower. The ground condenses into <<<image_6>>>, a cloth-and-tile fish writhing on the white floor. Stay long enough to read the mismatch of fish anatomy, fabric and tiled surfaces.
Pan up into <<<image_5>>>, the goat of household objects, erupting from a swirl of particulate matter and dashing across frame.
The heroine turns more quickly now, trying to see everything. The camera follows her turn, nearly losing focus, then catches her again.

16s–21s:
Rise upward with the orbit. Above her, <<<image_7>>> forms as a rotating spiral monument of human bodies. It turns in place, then starts coming apart at the edges into floating grains.
At nearly the same time, <<<image_8>>> lands delicately on the heroine’s head and vanishes a beat later.
Then <<<image_9>>> appears low and close: a rabbit with too many ears. The ears move independently like separate antennae. It hops away into the white.
Let the camera move from above-eye-level to near floor level in one continuous searching motion, keeping the heroine as the pivot point.

21s–26s:
The generative density spikes. <<<image_10>>> crosses the upper frame as a sheep-shaped cloud with internal lightning. <<<image_11>>>, a ball of birds, bursts through behind the heroine, moving as one compact flock-body. <<<image_12>>> resolves in a self-copying action: one horse becomes several adjacent repeating horses before the copies fail and shed back into dust.
On the ground, <<<image_13>>>, the pig of ears, briefly holds together, waddles and then slips apart into ear-like fragments.
The heroine continues turning in place, silent and alert, as if inside a storm of unfinished creation.

26s–30s:
The final wave arrives. <<<image_14>>>, the yellow-glove monkey, springs through the near field. <<<image_15>>> appears as a radish walking a dog across a small patch of white floor.
All around them, <<<image_17>>> through <<<image_28>>> manifest rapidly in fragments: badly generated people surround the heroine in a loose ring, some half-resolved, some with duplicate fingers, warped limbs, double faces, incorrect symmetry, clothes that reassemble and slide. They do not attack, they simply appear as a crowd of failed human generations and then lose definition.
The camera comes closest to <<<image_1>>> at the end, orbit tightening around her face while the swarm flickers in and out behind her. End with her still turning in the white ether as new grains begin forming more bodies just beyond full visibility.

Lighting:
Single practical source feeling, no fill, underexposed by a stop, dense smoky pale shadows inside the forms, compressed midtones, soft highlight rolloff with local clipping in the brightest white particulate field, slight exposure drift through the take.

Color:
Base: chalk white, milk-grey, pale dust.
Secondary: muted flesh, weak clay, fabric, ceramic and organic browns.
Accent: small sudden color incidents from individual references only, especially yellow glove material and minor color traces inside select creatures.
Dye-density color, one dominant pale field with sparse cutting accents, matte finish, heavy muted midtones.

Camera & optics:
One continuous handheld orbit, closer and more unstable than Version A. The camera circles the heroine tightly at first, then expands and contracts, diving to the floor for the fish and rabbit, lifting for the body-vortex and sheep-cloud, then returning to her face. It should feel like a witness inside a living denoising field, constantly trying to refind the subject. Focus searches, briefly resolves and drifts. No stabilization polish.
Old uncoated lens, low microcontrast, veiling glare in bright whites, spherical-aberration softness, faint chromatic fringing, living 16mm grain, uneven and thicker in the shadows, mild print flicker, slight irregular film weave.

Audio:
No music, no BGM, no score.
No dialogue, no speech.

0:06–0:09 particulate assembly and irregular multi-hoof impacts from the flawed horse.
0:08–0:11 a low internal glow-hum from the luminous figure.
0:11–0:14 damp cloth-and-tile flops from the fish.
0:12–0:15 object-clatter and light scraping from the household goat.

Keep the setting as an endless white generative field only.
Keep every figure appearing by particulate condensation, never by fade.
Keep a very high density of manifestations around the heroine.
Keep the heroine as the still center of the event while the camera and the world circle.
Keep the badly generated people as brief unstable manifestations rather than principal characters.

6s–12s:

The monkey lands on the intact left chair, balances there for a beat, turns toward <<<image_1>>> and gives one short sharp animal cry, like a scolding call, not speech.
It immediately leaps down and bounds into the open wall gap on the left.

12s–18s:
At 0:12.5 <<<image_3>>> emerges from the white ether. It is playful and energetic. It circles <<<image_1>>> in a loose excited path, hopping and changing direction. It barks four times, but its mouth stays closed; every bark comes from inside the brass horn, and the thin rim visibly vibrates.
The camera dips and pivots around them, sometimes too close, sometimes slightly late, briefly losing focus as the dog passes near the lens.
At 0:15.5 <<<image_5>>> bursts out of the white field behind it: small, pink-tinted, badly generated, exactly three legs, crooked body, asymmetric face. It barks normally with its mouth, jumps around the horn-dog once, then springs directly into the horn opening of <<<image_3>>>.
The horn-dog jolts, both creatures turn as one and dash into the wall opening on the left.
The camera snaps after them but never fully catches the exit.

At 0:26.5 <<<image_1>>> starts walking toward the white field.
The camera follows closely, becoming more intimate. She raises her hand and touches the surface of the ether. It behaves like dense generative atmosphere, suspended paint-dust, a soft unfinished medium.
Do not make her disintegrate. She stays physically intact.
She leans in, then steps into it. Move to a close view of her face and upper body entering the white generative space. Her whole body goes inside as a solid person entering deep fog or fluid light, not dissolving into particles. Her silhouette becomes increasingly obscured by the density of the ether, but she remains whole.
End at 0:30 with the camera holding on the pale field where she has entered, the right chair still mutating faintly in the background.

MANIFESTATION LAW — applies to everything that comes into existence in this shot.
Nothing fades in, dissolves in, assembles from particles, flies in, or emerges from smoke or light. The thing is already in its final position, at its final size, in the very first frame — only unresolved. What changes is not its presence but its resolution.
The noise is the substance of the image itself, never an overlay on top of a finished frame: at every moment the frame is a complete, internally consistent image at its own level of resolution.
Resolution happens in visible discrete steps, not as a smooth fade. The image holds still, then jumps to a more resolved state, holds, jumps again — six to eight jumps in total, each smaller and closer to the last, so the process decelerates toward the end.
Order of resolution runs from low frequency to high:
1. raw boiling coloured static, the shape of nothing;
2. large soft masses of light and shadow and one dominant colour — the composition is already readable while nothing is identifiable;
3. silhouettes and edges — objects become nameable but not yet material;
4. material and texture — fabric weave, wood grain, dust, skin;
5. the smallest high-contrast details last — fingers, eyelashes, chandelier drops, buttons, small metal.
Hands and faces resolve last and worst. Contact shadows and reflections arrive one step behind the object that casts them, so for one beat the thing stands without its shadow. Deep shadow areas never finish resolving at all: raw boiling noise stays visible there for the rest of the shot, as if that part of the world is still rendering.

Summary: a first-person observer crosses a palace-office seam, investigates chairs, window and flickering office light, then passes through self-opening doors into a regenerated silent-film chamber where the world around them cycles through archetypal but imperfect memories of great old cinema.

0s–6s: Start near the left side of the room, already moving forward. The observer sees the seam clearly: parquet on the left turning into office carpet on the right, chandelier hanging over a space partly claimed by fluorescent ceiling tiles. Fluorescent panels begin a behavioral glitch rather than a brightness effect: one panel flickers late, one panel remains dark, another lights with a one-second delay after the observer looks up. The clock on the far wall is visible at 10:10. The chairs wait in the right half of the room.

6s–12s: Turn right and approach the chairs. Hold on them. Instead of dramatic motion, the chairs regenerate through subtle office-world errors. The nearest chair’s armrests do not match: the right armrest is slightly lower than the left and seems to belong to a different model. A rear chair rotates just enough to face the observer without its wheels moving. Another chair briefly tries to become a duplicate of the nearest chair, then settles back into its own position. A caster base almost resolves as five spokes, then returns to four. At 0:10 the room tone splice is audible as the farthest chair finishes its silent turn.

12s–18s: Walk toward the windows and stop. Look out. The exterior is a layered archive of incompatible urban memory. Through one pane there is a foggy European boulevard with tram wires and no people. Through the next pane, an empty office district courtyard with strip-lit windows and no visible movement. Through the third pane, the outside has already slipped into early cinema: an expressionist street corner with exaggerated shadows and undercranked pedestrians who do not quite touch the ground correctly. Looking away and back does not unify them. Each pane keeps its own world. Window light remains the dominant illumination inside.

18s–22s: Turn toward the double doors and walk to them. Before the observer reaches the handles, the doors open by themselves inward. The space beyond is pure silent-film density: blackness, an arched doorway, the pale long-fingered figure of <<<image_2>>>, and a motion style that already feels older than the room behind. Cross the threshold. During the crossing, the image does not receive a superficial retro effect; instead, the world itself changes stock and time behavior: orthochromatic-looking pale skin, heavy black clothing, increased film weave, harder contrast, slight undercranked step cadence, and simpler gesture language.

22s–30s: Once inside, do not focus only on the central figure. The observer slowly looks around while the entire environment rerolls through a succession of famous-old-cinema memories that are recognizable in spirit but never exact replicas. The figure in the doorway remains a stable anchor while the room beyond changes. First the architecture becomes a crooked cabinet-like expressionist chamber. Then it becomes a broad hall with looming machine silhouettes and posed workers. Then a gothic staircase where an unnaturally long shadow climbs before the body does. Then a theatrical crypt-like set with candelabra and frontal actors. Then a city street with flattened perspective and a crowd posed like an early actuality film. Each regenerated image lasts about one second and is slightly wrong in composition, scale or body logic, as though cinema history itself is being remembered by a faulty model. End with the observer standing within this unstable archive, looking into yet another half-formed silent tableau.

Lighting: in the opening room, dominant window light from the left, no fill, underexposed by half to one stop, dense smoky shadows in the office side, compressed midtones, local clipping near shutters, slow exposure drift. Fluorescent panels on the office side are practicals and may flicker or lag in response, but they never flatten the room. After the doorway, the lighting becomes hard, sparse and stage-like, with pale faces and hands emerging from deep black space.

Color: opening room base is dusty blue-grey and old cream with muted gold moulding; secondary charcoal office tones; accent is cold white window spill. After the threshold, the world drains into dirty sepia, black and chalky ivory, matte and high-density.

Camera & optics: first-person handheld witness, slow human pace, restrained head turns, no stabilization, no float. Old uncoated lens, low microcontrast, veiling glare near windows, faint chromatic fringing, slight focus breathing, focus searching gently on chairs and window exteriors. Living 16mm grain, uneven and thicker in the shadows, subtly boiling over time, hand-processed texture, mild print flicker, slight irregular film weave. Inside the silent-film chamber, the weave becomes more pronounced and temporal cadence becomes mildly undercranked, but avoid novelty retro effects.

Audio: near-silence. no music, no BGM, no score. Opening ambience: empty-room air, intermittent fluorescent hum, soft footsteps alternating between wood and carpet, room tone loops every 10 seconds with audible seams at 0:10 and 0:20. At the window, each pane contributes its own faint exterior world: distant tram hum, HVAC courtyard noise, or hollow cart-and-street resonance. After the threshold, the ambience reduces to projector-like flutter, hollow interior reverb and dry step sounds. The silent-film world stays wordless and almost acoustically flattened.
